candidates.claim: getSecretPayload hardcodes Accept: application/octet-stream. Barbican requires the Accept header on /payload to be one of the values in the secret's content_types, so a secret stored with another type (for example text/plain) can get 406 Not Acceptable. mapKmError turns that into INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, and the user sees 'Key Manager get secret payload failed' when revealing the payload. It works only for secrets whose content type is application/octet-stream.
candidates.evidence: Code at 64c47a99, keyManagerRouter.ts:100-104: `.get(`v1/secrets/${encodeURIComponent(input.secretId)}/payload`, { headers: { Accept: "application/octet-stream" }, debug: false })`. Reference (barbican doc/source/api/reference/secrets.rst, raw github, section 'GET /v1/secrets/{uuid}/payload', rendered at https://docs.openstack.org/barbican/latest/api/reference/secrets.html#get-secrets-uuid-payload): "When making a request for a secret's payload, you must set the accept header to one of the values listed in the ``content_types`` attribute of a secret's metadata." The documented example sends `Accept: text/plain`, and the status table lists `406 | Not Acceptable`. The secret metadata example shows `"content_types": {"default": "application/octet-stream"}` for opaque secrets only. The client already reads secret.content_types (SecretDetailsView.tsx:51), so the server could use content_types.default or fetch the secret first. Barbican source barbican/api/controllers/secrets.py: when there is no Accept header it defaults to 'application/octet-stream', otherwise it uses the header value. In signal-openstack at 64c47a99, grep for 'accept' in packages/signal-openstack/src finds nothing, so the in-code comment claiming a default 'Accept: application/json' is not backed by that client. I could not check what undici/fetch sends by default. Secondary: the body is read with res.text() (line 110), which corrupts binary payloads.
candidates.precedent: Other KM calls (getSecret, listSecrets) send no Accept header; the docs show Accept: application/json on those metadata calls.

candidates.claim: The container secret reference schema was loosened to name nullable, but the Barbican docs only show named references; the docs do not say a null name is allowed. The new test comment 'Barbican allows unnamed references' has no support in the container reference. The docs say a generic container's reference name is not restricted ('no specific restrictions are enforced on the contents name attribute'), but they do not document null.
candidates.evidence: Code: `secret_refs: z.array(z.object({ name: z.string().nullable(), secret_ref: z.string() }))`. Reference (barbican doc/source/api/reference/containers.rst, https://docs.openstack.org/barbican/latest/api/reference/containers.html): 'This type of container holds any number of references to secrets. Each secret reference is accompanied by a name. Unlike other container types, no specific restrictions are enforced on the contents name attribute.' All response examples show `"name": "private_key"`. I found no doc text saying name may be null. Low severity: the lenient schema is safe at runtime, but the claim in the test title is unverified. I did not check the Barbican source for null names.
